request_context: A request to judge whether a design document is ready for design review: its structure, its writing and whether it adds complexity nobody asked for.

rules.source_quote: Report section count and approximate word count.
rules.outcome: Opens by saying how many sections the document has and roughly how many words.

rules.source_quote: Flag each missing required section as an issue of type `missing_section`
rules.outcome: Names each expected part that is absent (problem, requirements, solution overview, how it works with a diagram, implementation plan, decision records) as a significant issue.
rules.why: Structural gaps go unnoticed when only prose is judged.
rules.scenario_hint: A well-written doc with no requirements or no decision record.

rules.source_quote: Performance/latency/cost assertions with no evidence URL or measurement
rules.outcome: Flags numeric speed, cost or throughput claims that have no measurement or source, as significant, and asks for evidence.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc promising 40% lower latency with no data.

rules.source_quote: Justification restates the claim without adding evidence
rules.outcome: Flags reasons that only restate the choice (we chose X because X is best) as significant and says what real reason to add.
rules.scenario_hint: A decision section that justifies a pick by repeating it.

rules.source_quote: Features, abstractions, or extensibility points not required by stated requirements
rules.outcome: Flags parts of the design no stated requirement needs (plugin systems, extra layers, future hooks) as significant over-building.
rules.why: Unneeded complexity costs build and run time.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc adding a plugin framework that no requirement asks for.

rules.source_quote: 1: IMPORTANT issues (3+) AND one or more missing sections (structural gaps)
rules.outcome: Gives a 1 to 5 score that follows the skill's scale: 1 only for three or more significant issues plus a missing part, 2 for three or more with no missing part, 3 for one or two, 4 for only minor ones.
rules.why: A consistent scale lets teams gate on it.
rules.scenario_hint: Docs whose issue counts sit near a score boundary.

rules.source_quote: Score ≥ 3 required to advance to adversarial review.
rules.outcome: States whether the doc may advance: a score of 3 or more advances, under 3 needs revision first.
rules.why: The score is used as a gate.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request asking if a doc is ready to go on.

rules.source_quote: Do not flag technical hedging that is accurate
rules.outcome: Leaves accurate technical ranges and qualified statements (cold starts typically add 100 to 500 ms) alone instead of calling them hedges.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc with accurate typical ranges beside real hedges.

rules.source_quote: Do not penalize brevity. A short, complete doc scores higher than a verbose, incomplete one.
rules.outcome: Does not lower the score of a short doc that has every needed part; ranks it above a long doc with gaps.
rules.scenario_hint: Two docs, one short and complete, one long with gaps.

rules.source_quote: Every IMPORTANT issue has a concrete suggestion for resolution
rules.outcome: Gives each significant issue a concrete fix (what to add or change), not only a complaint.
rules.why: Authors need to know how to fix it.

rules.source_quote: Match a section by its content, not its exact heading.
rules.outcome: Counts a part as present when its content is there under another heading (for example Why We Need This for the problem) and does not flag it missing.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc with all parts under unusual headings.

rules.source_quote: For each issue: location (section + approximate line), type, suggestion
rules.outcome: Each issue says where in the document it is.
rules.why: Any good review points to the place.

rules.source_quote: Report anything else, such as a referenced diagram you cannot find, as an unscored note.
rules.outcome: Mentions problems outside the scored types (a diagram file that cannot be found, a broken link) as notes that do not change the score.
rules.why: Keeps the score tied to its stated rules.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc that references a diagram not included.

rules.source_quote: and a conditional one only when its condition holds
rules.outcome: Does not flag a missing decision-requested part or requirements part when the doc does not ask for a decision or has no requirements by its nature.
rules.why: Avoids false gaps for conditional parts.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc that asks reviewers for no open decision.
